clue.text: Graduates consuming soft rolls

indicators.note: the graduates eat, so hold, the next piece inside them

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, university graduates
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Some graduates eating soft bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft, flat bread rolls in British baking.

clue.text: .Reddish firearm duke kept in northern town

indicators.note: the gun and duke are held within the town's name

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, northern England
a gun is a firearm

explanation.surface: A reddish gun belonging to a duke is kept in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop before 'Reddish' is a print mark. BURY is a mill town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgundy is the deep purplish-red colour named after the wine, so it describes something reddish.

clue.text: Sort of seahorse odd person found under cask

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: a pipe is a large cask for wine or port
a queer or odd fish is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: A peculiar person is discovered beneath a barrel, like some seahorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipefish are slender fish of the same family as seahorses, so loosely a sort of seahorse.

clue.text: But this assistant wouldn't give away baby frame!

definitions.text: But this assistant wouldn't give away baby frame!

parts.words: But this assistant wouldn't give away baby frame!
parts.note: to shop is to betray, and a baby's walking frame is a walker; this store assistant's title read as 'betray a walker' is something they would never do

explanation.surface: A store worker refusing to hand over a child's walking frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopwalker was a supervising assistant in a department store who walked the floor helping customers.

clue.text: Pierced side of cargo area, say

indicators.note: 'say' signals that the word is spoken, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: the hold is the cargo-carrying part of a ship below the decks

explanation.surface: A ship's hull breached at the side where the cargo is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Holed means having a hole made in it, the same as pierced or punctured.

clue.text: Eliot is one, by George!

parts.note: 'by George!' looks like an exclamation, but George Eliot was the pen name Mary Ann Evans wrote under

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming in surprise about the poet Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is a pen name, as George Eliot was for novelist Mary Ann Evans.

clue.text: Training aid a sailor of bawdy type reportedly used?

indicators.note: 'reportedly' signals that the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a salt is a sailor, and coarse means bawdy, giving 'a salt coarse'

explanation.surface: A vulgar seaman makes use of some training equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a salt coarse' matches the military obstacle course.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault course is an obstacle course on which soldiers are trained.

clue.text: Water spirit that's found under seaweed

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece is placed below the first

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A water sprite lurking beneath the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: A kelpie is a shape-shifting water spirit of Scottish folklore, often a horse.

clue.text: Campanologist's double

definitions.meaning: someone who sounds church bells, often in a team pulling ropes in a tower
a person who looks exactly like another

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer's lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringer rings church bells, and a ringer is also a close lookalike or substitute.

clue.text: The rest rejected bribe in Brazilian money

indicators.note: the turned bribe goes inside the currency

parts.note: the real is Brazil's currency

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

explanation.surface: The remainder turned down a bribe paid in Brazilian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' signals the bribe word is read backwards; a sop was originally bread dipped in liquid, later anything offered to placate.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposal is an old word for repose, meaning rest.

clue.text: Soldiers do it, beating up old fogeys

definitions.meaning: drill on the parade ground, which soldiers do
bashing squares, squares being stuffy conventional people

explanation.surface: Troops are given to assaulting elderly bores.
explanation.definitionFit: Square-bashing is slang for military drill on a parade square.

clue.text: Greek character's name given to old record store

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record, an old format
a silo is a store for grain

explanation.surface: A Greek person's name is given to a former record shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a Greek character.

clue.text: Lacking finance to secure ring? It's not established

indicators.note: the unfunded word holds the ring inside it

parts.note: unfunded means without money provided
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Without the money to buy a ring, an engagement isn't settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfounded means having no basis, so not established in fact.

clue.text: Make one free, reversing the indictment, initially

indicators.note: the two initial letters are swapped round in the word for free

parts.note: untie means set free

indicators.note: the first letters of the words the and indictment are taken

explanation.surface: Join together and liberate someone by overturning the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T and I; 'reversing' turns the TI in UNTIE into IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join things together so that they become one.

clue.text: Single out one man involved in underworld wrongdoing

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself

indicators.note: the one and the man are wrapped up inside the wrongdoing

parts.note: crime is wrongdoing
I is the Roman numeral one
Nat is a man's name

explanation.surface: Picking out a single man mixed up in gangland crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to distinguish or pick something out from others.

clue.text: One may be stony and down-to earth

definitions.text: One may be stony and down-to earth

parts.words: One may be stony and down-to earth
parts.note: reads like a description of a stern, practical person, but describes a rock from space that is stony and comes down to earth

explanation.surface: A hard-faced yet practical person.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorite is a lump from space reaching the ground, many of them classified as stony.

clue.text: Gave support to small sibling involved in stormy dates

indicators.note: the sibling goes inside the rearranged dates
stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters are tossed about

parts.note: sis is the shortened form of sister

explanation.surface: Helping a little sister through some turbulent romantic evenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges the letters of dates, and 'involved in' puts the sibling inside them after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisted means helped, so gave support to someone.

clue.text: Shy characters primarily engaged for similar roles

indicators.note: the characters come first, ahead of the throw

parts.note: type means printed characters
to shy is to throw, and so is to cast

explanation.surface: Timid actors chiefly hired to play the same kind of part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid but means throw, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A typecast actor is repeatedly given the same kind of part.

clue.text: Cook I mostly abuse in sober manner

indicators.note: to cook is to falsify or doctor, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef admits to mostly misusing drink, while staying sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemiously means with restraint in eating and drinking, temperately or soberly.

clue.text: Mountain. guide keeping woman in Belgian 'town

indicators.note: the town's name holds the woman inside it

parts.note: Spa is a resort town in Belgium
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A mountain guide looks after a lady in a Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop and apostrophe are print marks. SPA, the Belgian town, gave its name to all spas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as guides and porters on mountain expeditions.

clue.text: Mouthful of fungus son swallowed

indicators.note: the fungus takes the son inside it

parts.note: a morel is an edible fungus

explanation.surface: A son gulps down a bite of mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bite or mouthful of food.

clue.text: Roars with laughter, provoking expression of irritation

definitions.meaning: a Scottish exclamation of impatience, '..., mon!'

explanation.surface: Someone laughs loudly, prompting annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoots are loud laughs, and hoots is also a Scots interjection of annoyance.

clue.text: Entrance to oratory, where it's reconstructed differently

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter
reconstructed means rebuilt, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The doorway of a chapel where it has been rebuilt in another way.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in a different way, differently.

clue.text: Go away from house overlooking mine

indicators.note: in a down answer the house sits above the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Leave the house that stands above the colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is British slang telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Composer and Antarctic explorer in one

parts.note: James Clark Ross explored the Antarctic, giving his name to the Ross Sea
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man who is both a composer and a polar explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Handy devices for plucky players

parts.note: plucky seems to mean brave, but here the players pluck strings, using small devices held in the hand

explanation.surface: Useful gadgets for courageous sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectra are picks held in the hand to pluck the strings of guitars and similar instruments.

clue.text: Singer traps bird by lake fairly quickly

indicators.note: the singer catches the lake and bird inside

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
an egret is a heron-like bird

explanation.surface: A singer catches a bird beside a lake rather quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is the musical direction for a fairly brisk tempo, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Italian fellow primarily employed to amend copy

indicators.note: the fellow is used first, placed ahead of the Italian

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, a fellow
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian man is taken on mainly to correct text.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise or correct written material.
